entries.grounds: Confirmed: inside() (cli_invocation.py:948) `[spec.origin] if spec.origin and spec.has_location else ...` with the `and` operands swapped to `spec.has_location and spec.origin`. The expression's value is used ONLY as the truth condition of a conditional-expression, and bool(A and B) == bool(B and A) for all A,B (AND truth value is commutative), so the SAME branch is taken in every case regardless of spec type. spec.origin (plain attr) and spec.has_location (ModuleSpec property returning self._set_fileattr, a bool) are side-effect-free, so swapping evaluation order cannot raise or differ. EQUIVALENT by code (simpler and more general than the author's PathFinder enumeration, which is sound corroboration). Not separately measured (pure boolean-commutativity proof); the campaign measured SURVIVED.
entries.note: the author's PathFinder (T,F)/(F,T) analysis is correct but unnecessary: commutativity of the AND truth value settles it for any spec.

entries.grounds: Confirmed: conclude() (cli_invocation.py:904) `said.acquire(blocking=False)`->`blocking=True`. said = threading.Lock() (883), acquired non-blocking in settle(901) and conclude(904) and NEVER released (no said.release in the HARNESS, grep). conclude is reached ONLY from the daemon Timer built in deadline()(908, timer.daemon=True, never joined/cancelled). When the lock is FREE (deadline wins the race) both acquire at once and write RESULT(deadline)/END identically; when HELD (the subject already settled) the non-blocking call returns False and writes nothing, the blocking call parks forever and also writes nothing -- the acquire is atomic either way, so the RESULT winner, protocol file and exit status are identical. The only difference is a parked daemon thread, which is not a range member and is not read by the parent (_watch reads the protocol file and the range's wait status); interpreter shutdown abandons daemon threads. EQUIVALENT by code (author's park.py measurement corroborates equal exit time). Campaign measured SURVIVED.
entries.note: threading.Lock is non-reentrant and never released; conclude's sole caller is the daemon timer.
